answer: Settlement drops a second key that reuses a clearing seat. Each address may hold only one seat on the saffron book. Mid-epoch that seat must sign a margin pulse mixing the seed with the summit auction fix; a replay fails because the seat-and-nonce pair is consumed. Delivery uses one dock at a warehouse on the dune reserved for that seat, so two principals cannot share it. Clone cost rises linearly: another seat, another margin. Hypothetical costs: $1,800 a seat and $55 per pulse, so 100 clones spend $180,000 plus $5,500.
